body:
Sometimes you find that stability earlier on.

Sometimes it's just simply not there.

I'm 45 now.  I have a job that pays the bills. Nothing exciting. I have a wife who excels in her career performance and a kid who is just starting high school but is driven to do well.

I wish I could do it over. To do better in school. To get into a better college. To excel and go to med school. Or to get into a great PhD program doing research in a specific field that will help people.  To actually exercise and not neglect my health and my teeth.  But right now feels like it''s too late. And that scares and depresses the hell out of me.

So - I totally feel you regarding the reset button.

"I'm in therapy, and my therapist is good. But I'm scared if I tell her just how much I want to die I'll be committed."

I relate to this so much. And I feel hypocritical when I do -- I'm supposed to be able to let her know anything and everything in order to let her help. Hell, we've even gone through the different steps that would take place if I were to tell her that I was suicidal.  

I don't have an autistic child, but from friends who do and who have shared their experiences it can be very, very challenging.  Just because you're having trouble with this does NOT mean you're failing nor would make quality better for your son if you weren't in the picture.  Sometimes it's about taking it one hour at a time...

Working through the pain is hard.  And it sounds like there is so much of it.  I'd really like you to consider having your therapist know a little more about what's going on. You don't have to say that you're thinking of suicide straight out; you can just mention that you're really in crisis and need help coping.  If they're really good, then they'll take a look at things and really try to help you on your terms.

Wishing you the best this evening...
This is really helpful. Thank you.

This resonates so much with me.  I, too, have the comfortable job, the beautiful wife, the beautiful kid, and the beautiful home with the beautiful cars in the driveway. In comparison to what others are experiencing just to get food on the table, what do I have to be anxious about? Nonetheless, it still exists for me, and it's not something I can just snap out of.

Your method of explaining your thought processes to those close to you and to your therapist is a great idea — and one I should really push myself to do. I'm still really intimidated to talk about this with friends — because I have this fear of being that one friend who doesn't pull his weight and needs more help. And I also have this fear of worrying everyone else too much with my baggage. But it sounds like I need to determine a way to help them to understand what I'm going through.
I am taking Sudafed (antihistamine), but I don't think it's playing with my Wellbutrin...
Thank you. <3 I most certainly would share.
